analysis:
Examined provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop.swift. Changed head ranges are 781-792 (new actor state: selectedModelRecovery, selectedModelRecoveryLoadOverride, savedEnabledModels, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch) and 954 (savedEnabledModels initialised from config.config.backend.enabledModels). The supplied head excerpt covers only lines 1-532, so the changed lines at 781-792 and 954 are not visible as numbered text, only in the patch. The base unit (lines 1024-1290) is unchanged context.

The visible diff only adds in-memory actor stored properties and one init assignment. It touches no attestation, App Attest authorization, encryption, key custody, cache storage, coordinator wire, or add-on socket code. A test-only load override is internal and nil in production. No new trust boundary, data exposure or authorization path is introduced here.

Remaining integration questions, which sit in other files not supplied: ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery (not seen) implements the recovery that reloads selected models. It should be checked for (a) bypassing memory admission, eviction and fleet-budget gates (TB-007, T-029); (b) respecting add-on holds (TB-012, T-059), so recovery does not load models beside running VMs; (c) honouring the attestation/App Attest serving authorization and drain state before advertising; (d) not re-advertising models retired by a failed self-test (failedSelfTestHashes, retiringModels). Also check how savedEnabledModels is refreshed from the config file by the policy refresh and whether that can alter the serving set without a committed switch. T-041 (cache) is not affected by this hunk. No finding is raised from the supplied evidence.
